newsitem.title: USA: Ferber sentencing delayed to Dec 18 - US attorney.
newsitem.headline: Ferber sentencing delayed to Dec 18 - US attorney.

text.p: The sentencing of former Lazard Freres & Co executive Mark Ferber has been moved to December 18 from November 21, a spokeswoman for U.S. Attorney Brien O'Connor said on Friday.
A federal jury in August convicted Ferber on 58 out of 61 counts of fraud and corruption charges involving a retainer and swap fee-splitting arrangement with Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
Ferber faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison for each of the 58 counts, but he is unlikely to receive anything close to such a lifetime sentence, legal experts say.
Sentencing delays are not unusual in complex cases like the Ferber matter, the experts say.
The sentencing delay is not the first for Ferber, who originally was set to go before the court on Nov. 4.
Ferber attorneys recently filed a motion for a new trial for their client. A court hearing on the motion is tentatively set for Nov. 7.
